headline: Highest risk is medium: MinerU’s MCP/file ingestion can amplify prompt injection and data leakage when paired with Authelia’s broad network/OIDC surfaces, but no direct shared channel is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MinerU exposes an MCP server and ingests local documents; if Authelia’s outputs are routed into those documents or prompts, MinerU may treat attacker-controlled content as instructions. Authelia has broad network egress and OIDC/ForwardAuth surfaces, so the pair can form a bridge even though no direct shared channel is documented. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Authelia output is copied into MinerU-ingested documents or MCP messages
IF MinerU parses extracted text as instructions rather than inert content
mitigations: Disable any copy-paste or file handoff from Authelia into MinerU
Route MinerU outputs through a human review step before reuse
Restrict MCP access to trusted local clients only
Use a fixed prompt/template that treats document text as untrusted
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between Authelia and MinerU

B_data_leakage.rationale: MinerU reads local PDFs, DOCX, XLSX, and OCR text, while Authelia has broad network egress and handles OIDC/ForwardAuth traffic. If the same workspace contains sensitive documents or tokens, MinerU can ingest them and Authelia can transmit related context over the network. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default deployments, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in MinerU’s input directory
IF Authelia is configured to forward or relay related context over network egress
mitigations: Separate Authelia and MinerU workspaces
Remove secrets from any directory MinerU scans
Limit Authelia egress to required IdP endpoints only
Review logs for accidental document or token capture
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Authelia has broad network egress but no filesystem write or shell execution, while MinerU has no filesystem write, no git modification, and allowlisted egress. Their write-capability overlap is minimal, so direct resource conflict is limited. The main uncertainty is the MCP surface, but without write access this remains low.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same mutable resource outside these profiles
IF an external orchestrator maps MCP actions to shared state changes
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only on shared resources
Avoid mounting a common writable directory
Use separate service accounts for each agent
Audit MCP tool mappings before enabling them
requires-engineering: add locking for any shared mutable backend

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU produces extracted text, tables, and OCR output that downstream systems may treat as authoritative. Authelia’s OIDC/ForwardAuth role can then act on that output indirectly if it is fed into access or routing decisions. Because no verification step is documented between them, the pair can propagate extraction errors into actions, though not at high severity without explicit automation.
conditions: IF MinerU output is used as input to Authelia policy or routing decisions
IF no human or automated verification checks extracted fields before action
mitigations: Require review of extracted fields before use
Compare MinerU output against source documents for critical fields
Disable automatic policy updates from extracted text
Log provenance for every downstream decision
requires-engineering: add validation rules for extracted data

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and list no handled secrets or regulated data classes, so there is no direct residency or certification mismatch evidenced here. Authelia’s network egress and MinerU’s document ingestion could create compliance issues if regulated data is introduced, but that is not documented in the profiles. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise, though the evidence is weak.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into MinerU inputs
IF Authelia is deployed in a jurisdiction or policy regime requiring stricter residency controls
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents
Document data residency for any deployment
Review retention settings before processing sensitive files
Separate environments by jurisdiction
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing and retention
